The injection point never stalls: the network has no flow control, and a full output FIFO is an overflow (condition 1, figure 4.3).
B. Reads from any chunk (§4.1: no alignment): one or two rows, merged into the slot in order
Chunks are 32 bits, chunk 0 is bits [31:0] of a row and of the slot. Green: part 0 (row r); blue: part 1 (row r + 1, the next area when r is an area's last row).
A read covering two rows costs two area
accesses and holds its token until both
are in; the packets are the same as for
C. Out-of-order returns, in-order packets: four 64-bit reads to areas 2, 5, 2, 7 (one row each)
Tag 1 returns first but waits in its slot; tag 0's return (t+4) lets the head go at t+5, then 1 and 2 follow one a cycle (3 at t+8).
A slot is valid from the end of its last part's return cycle; the head is injected the next cycle (one register stage).
taken this cycle; tail is its tag

the holding register was injected this cycle
dst 7, mode 4, addr 20, payload 64; the router adds src
• The token FIFO absorbs a read's queueing at its area; how much a phase's placement needs is still open (§4.2), and 64 entries is the depth (§10).
• In HALT the token FIFO is held empty (§4.5); no packet is in flight when RUN/HALT changes.
Every read taken pushes a token whose tail index is the read's tag. A read may start at any chunk: its one or two rows return in any order and are
merged into its slot in order; the head leaves when both parts are in, as one packet (two for 128 bits), so packets trail the requests in request
order. The injection point takes a return packet whenever one is ready, and the send port's packet otherwise.
